stem: A client deliberately falsifies or induces signs of illness. Assessment identifies no apparent external incentive such as financial compensation, avoiding legal or work obligations, housing, or obtaining medications. Which condition is most consistent with this pattern?
rationale: Factitious disorder imposed on self involves intentional production or falsification of physical or psychological symptoms without external incentives. Malingering also involves intentional fabrication or exaggeration, but it is motivated by external gain. Somatic symptom disorder and illness anxiety disorder do not require intentional deception. Therefore A is the best answer.
educational_objective: Differentiate factitious disorder from malingering and nondeceptive somatic symptom-related conditions by the presence of intentional falsification and external incentives.
source_version_date: Factitious Disorder updated July 7, 2025; Malingering updated April 12, 2026
source_locator: Factitious Disorder — Continuing Education Activity, Introduction, Differential Diagnosis; Malingering — Continuing Education Activity, Introduction, Differential Diagnosis
source_claim_supported: Factitious disorder involves intentional falsification or induction of illness without external incentives; malingering involves intentional fabrication/exaggeration for external incentives; somatic symptom and illness-anxiety presentations do not depend on intentional deception.
blueprint_locator: Psychosocial Integrity — recognition of psychiatric and somatic symptom-related disorders
correction_summary: Converted the original definition-style options into parallel diagnostic labels and independently cross-checked malingering against its April 2026 StatPearls update. Avoided requiring proof of a specific internal motive or 'sick role'; absence of apparent external incentives plus intentional falsification is the tested distinction. Difficulty set to medium.
audit_findings: Current NCBI sources directly support A and distinguish it from malingering by external incentive. C and D do not require intentional fabrication. Independent second pass challenged the key against all three distractors and found no second defensible answer.
